gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-puritan: Tilt Neon draws each letter as a tube of constant width, with a splayed c terminal and short ascenders. Puritan follows with rounded, open forms and oversized counters in e and a, so paragraphs feel friendly and unhurried.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-radio-canada: A splayed c terminal gives Tilt Neon its tube-lit attitude. It earns its keep big and short, while Radio Canada, a sans-serif with tall, full lowercase c, s and z, carries the rest with a steady line.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-radio-canada-big: Bold tube-like strokes of constant width give Tilt Neon a large x-height and short ascenders. Radio Canada Big settles into a monoline plain sans, its terminals finishing well away from the stem, so lines glide along comfortably.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-readex-pro: The tube-like, constant-width stroke of Tilt Neon is what you notice first. It does loud and large best, while Readex Pro does quiet, unvarying running text best, with broad gaps at its terminals.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-savate: Commanding and marker-like, Tilt Neon holds one constant-width line. Savate, with open jaws and a tall rounded o, brings a moderate, swelling stroke that makes the marker line feel deliberate.
gen-gf-offside-gf-vend-sans: Loose, wide, and defiantly open, Offside spreads out. It is built for big display moments, while Vend Sans, with its ruler-drawn line and wide, unclosed curve endings, handles the reading.
gen-gf-goldman-gf-sono: Goldman is all wide stance and parenthesis-round curves, built to command a headline. And Sono, whose lowercase stands tall and whose letters sit well apart, handles the quieter job of running text.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-stack-sans-headline: Tube-bright strokes, one width throughout, make Tilt Neon impossible to miss. Stack Sans Headline keeps a monoline skeleton and a deep middle band, and that shared constant line is what ties them together.
gen-gf-turret-road-archivo: Round and pen-drawn, Turret Road keeps a constant weight like open parentheses. Archivo then adds a commanding x-height and outward-opening curves, so words stand taller than the moderate lowercase above them.
gen-gf-turret-road-fs-merriweather-sans: Turret Road draws round, parenthesis-like forms with a hairline-free, swell-free pen line. Merriweather Sans sits beside it taller and sturdier in the lowercase, with an e that opens clearly to the right, keeping the feel clean.
